label: Index pushdown (the family)
type: the FAMILY TERM for any work the Query service delegates to the Index service so it need not be done after the fetch. Members promoted separately: index:predicate-pushdown, index:pagination-pushdown, index:order-pushdown, index:index-projection, index:group-aggregate-pushdown, index:operator-pushdown. NOT the same as index:covering-index (which eliminates the fetch entirely rather than moving work into it) and NOT the same as early filtering (which is the Query service doing the work EARLY, precisely because it could not be pushed down).
recurrence_note: Six files, undiscounted. `index_pushdowns.md` exists three times, so shared-source.py checked whether the six collapse to three - and returned `divergent`: quotes supporting this id sit on one copy and on no sibling, so a second author really wrote them. The discount is rejected and the count stands at 6.
note:
PROMOTED, AND IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION ROUND 17 WAS DISPATCHED TO ASK. Rounds 11-16 kept meeting individual pushdowns at recurrence 1-3 with no page that recognised them as a family, and repeatedly deferred the family term for want of a definition. `index_pushdowns.md` is that page - the family is its title, its lede and its six H2 headings - and it had never been extracted in the server tree. The family was not undocumented; it was unread.
THE FAMILY IS DEFINED TWICE, WHICH IS WHY NO SINGLE COUNT FOUND IT. `groupby-aggregate-performance.md` also claims the family in its own abstract, classing itself as a SQL++ pushdown, while `index_pushdowns.md` mentions grouping and aggregate pushdown only under Related Links. So each of the two pages presents itself as the family's home and treats the other as a sibling topic. Two overlapping definitions is not the same as one definition, and a recurrence count cannot tell the difference - it sees a term used, not a term owned.
SCOPE WARNING FOR ANYONE QUERYING THIS: the six members are not a closed set stated anywhere. It is the union of what two pages enumerate. Nothing in the corpus says 'these are the pushdowns'.
relates_to_competency_question: What work does the Index service do on the Query service's behalf, and what is left over?
